description: Round 5's 'text over label' principle, applied naively to statement_type=='reopening' via admit_statement's asserts/admissibility, promotes LU 130 from unknown/low to closed/medium. Its reopening statement ("Please contact the office in January 2027 for information regarding the 2027-2028 school year.") lacks literal application-subject vocabulary and gets rejected no_application_subject, removing the block that round 1-4's rule 7 (CLOSED requires 'not reopening_statements') relies on -- even a vague, dateless reopening mention is meant to prevent a definitive 'closed' call. Worked around this round by leaving closed_statements/reopening_statements sourced on statement_type exactly as round 1-4 built them (not routed through asserts) rather than widening the subject vocabulary or weakening rule 7 under time pressure. Flagging so a future round can decide deliberately: either broaden APPLICATION_SUBJECT_WORDS to catch office-contact-for-reopening phrasing, or gate rule 7's reopening check on a narrower admissibility check that excludes only method/CTA/office-hours text, not subject vocabulary.
recommendation: Decide in a future round whether reopening statements should pass through any part of the admissibility gate

description: Same root cause as LU 130 in the other direction: the extractor emits the identical sentence twice under two different statement_type labels with two different stated_effective_date values specifically so a closed-copy and a reopening-copy can be told apart (LU 567: 'Applications ... are closed they will reopen November 2nd, 2026.' once as closed/stated_effective_date=null, once as reopening/stated_effective_date=2026-11-02). Deriving asserts from text collapses this distinction (both copies read as asserts=='closed', since the sentence contains the word 'closed') and misfiles the reopening date as a future CLOSURE date via the round-4 future-tense-closed branch -- the exact LU 466 bug reappearing. Left closed/reopening sourced on statement_type to sidestep this; a real fix would need to recognize same-text-different-structured-date duplication as a distinct extraction pattern.
recommendation: Consider a dedup/reconciliation pass in the extractor or in compute_status that recognizes duplicate verbatim_text across differently-labeled statements as intentional label pairs

description: LU 234 Castroville has a second admitted 'open'-labeled statement ("The JATC is currently accepting applications for the Inside Electrical Apprenticeship VIA MAIL ONLY. The office is not currently open for in-person applications.") that, read in isolation, contains an unambiguous 'currently accepting' state claim. It only resolves to asserts=='none' because of a general negation-detection rule (text containing both an open cue and a 'not currently open' negation is treated as self-contradictory/ambiguous) rather than because of any round-5-specific rule targeting this local. This is a reasonable general rule but the specific text is genuinely a coherent claim (mail applications open, in-person applications closed) that a more careful, method-vs-program-scoped read might resolve differently. Flagging as a judgment call rather than a settled fix.
recommendation: Revisit with a program/method-scoped read of mixed positive/negative statements if this pattern recurs elsewhere in the corpus.

LU 538 and LU 613 each pair a vague, undated 'open'-labeled statement (no embedded date in the statement's own text) with a real dated window whose close_date has already passed. Rule 4 (plain open statements) fires before rule 6 (expired_data from windows), so the vague statement's 'open' claim wins even though the window on the same record shows the intake period already ended months ago. This predates round 5 (present under the pre-round-5 compute_status.py too) and is out of scope for a demote-only round targeting the 'open' admissibility defect specifically, since fixing it requires reordering rules 4 and 6 -- a broader change with its own regression risk that wasn't validated against the full corpus in the time available this round.
column5: Consider a future round that cross-references an open statement's absence of its own embedded date against any window on the same record before trusting rule 4 over rule 6.
